title: Horizontal Positioning Fixture Hydraulic Requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: The topology implements the selected minimal conventional open-circuit hydraulic system. Tank feeds a fixed-displacement pump; pump pressure branches directly to the relief valve and the open-centre 4/3 DCV. Relief and DCV return ports terminate directly at the tank. The DCV work ports connect through the selected dual pilot-operated check/load-lock to the double-acting carriage cylinder, with the A-side feeding the cap chamber for advance and the B-side feeding the rod chamber for return. No flow-control component is added because advance and return speeds are sizing-only decisions. In neutral, the selected open-centre DCV vents A and B to tank while unloading P to T, allowing the pilot-operated check valve-side work lines to depressurize so the load-lock checks can reseat for low-leakage holding.

selected_components.name: Tank
selected_components.role: open-circuit reservoir for pump suction and all returns
configuration: Open-circuit tank boundary with suction outlet S and common return inlet R.

selected_components.name: Pump
configuration: Fixed-displacement supply; drive hardware and displacement are deferred to sizing.
Chosen for simplicity because no efficiency or standby unloading requirement is stated.
selected_components.selection_basis: Provides positive-displacement open-circuit supply with minimal complexity.

selected_components.name: Relief Valve
configuration: Pressure-limiting function to enforce the specified maximum system pressure of 100 bar during final setting/commissioning.
selected_components.selection_basis: Required to protect the open-circuit system from exceeding the specified pressure limit.

selected_components.name: 4/3 Solenoid DCV, Open Center
selected_components.role: operator-commanded advance, return and released neutral for carriage actuator
configuration: Extend state: P to A and B to T.
Retract state: P to B and A to T.
Neutral state: P, T, A and B interconnected, giving no commanded motion, pump unloading and pilot-line venting.
selected_components.selection_basis: Provides bidirectional cylinder control and a safe released neutral compatible with a fixed-displacement pump and pilot-check reseating.

selected_components.name: Dual Pilot-Operated Check Valve
configuration: Install between DCV work ports and both cylinder chambers, close to the actuator work ports.
Free flow from DCV side to actuator side on each work line.
Reverse flow from each actuator chamber is blocked until released by pressure in the opposite valve-side work line.
Neutral vents A1 and B1 through the open-centre DCV so pilot pressure decays and checks reseat.
selected_components.selection_basis: Satisfies the positive pilot-check load holding requirement for stopped-position negligible drift without relying on DCV spool sealing.

selected_components.name: Double-Acting Cylinder
configuration: Double-acting cylinder; bore, rod and 300 mm travel implementation are deferred to sizing.
Cap-end feed corresponds to carriage advance; rod-end feed corresponds to return.
selected_components.selection_basis: Required bidirectional linear actuator for horizontal carriage positioning.

connections.notes: Open-circuit reservoir suction supply to fixed-displacement pump.
Pump pressure branch to system pressure-limiting relief valve; branch is represented by repeated Pump.P endpoints.
Relieved flow returns directly to tank.
Pump pressure branch directly supplies the directional-control valve.
Directional-valve return and neutral unloading flow return directly to tank.
Advance-side valve-side work line. Pressure at A1 also provides the selected load-lock class's internal cross-pilot release for B2-to-B1 return flow during advance.
Advance-side actuator-side load-lock port connects directly to cylinder cap chamber.
Return-side valve-side work line. Pressure at B1 also provides the selected load-lock class's internal cross-pilot release for A2-to-A1 return flow during retraction.
Return-side actuator-side load-lock port connects directly to cylinder rod chamber.

motion_control_decisions.justification: The stated advance speed and force are sizing targets only; no adjustable or load-independent speed control is specified. Horizontal load is stated as resistance, so no dynamic load-control strategy is required during powered advance.

The stated return speed and force are sizing targets only; no adjustable or load-independent speed control is specified. Horizontal load is stated as resistance, so no dynamic load-control strategy is required during powered return.

Static retention is explicitly required at any stopped position with negligible drift under load. A static load-locking capability is required; the load is horizontal and not overrunning, so counterbalance behavior is not indicated.

component_states.reason: Selected catalog state internally connects P to A and B to T for cylinder cap-end supply and rod-end exhaust through the load lock.

phase_configurations.notes: In this phase, DCV.A pressurizes LoadLock.A1 for free flow A1-to-A2 to Cylinder.Cap. A1 pressure internally pilots the selected dual pilot-check to release Cylinder.Rod exhaust from B2 to B1, then through DCV.B to DCV.T and Tank.R.

component_states.reason: Selected catalog state internally connects P to B and A to T for cylinder rod-end supply and cap-end exhaust through the load lock.

phase_configurations.notes: In this phase, DCV.B pressurizes LoadLock.B1 for free flow B1-to-B2 to Cylinder.Rod. B1 pressure internally pilots the selected dual pilot-check to release Cylinder.Cap exhaust from A2 to A1, then through DCV.A to DCV.T and Tank.R.

component_states.reason: Selected open-centre neutral unloads P to T and vents A and B to T so LoadLock.A1 and LoadLock.B1 pilot pressure decays and the pilot-operated checks reseat.

phase_configurations.notes: Holding is provided by the dual pilot-operated check valve blocking reverse flow from both actuator chambers while the open-centre DCV vents the valve-side work/pilot lines to tank.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S and Pump.P provides the open-circuit pressure source for the relief branch and carriage DCV branch. Pump displacement and drive details remain sizing tasks.
Pump.P connects directly to ReliefValve.P and ReliefValve.T returns to Tank.R. The relief setting is to be commissioned to enforce the specified 100 bar maximum system pressure.

DCV extend state routes pump flow to the cap-side branch for carriage advance and rod-side exhaust to tank. DCV retract state routes pump flow to the rod-side branch for return and cap-side exhaust to tank. The Cylinder converts hydraulic power to bidirectional linear carriage motion.

LoadLock blocks reverse flow from both actuator chambers in the stopped condition. The DCV neutral state vents A and B through T to Tank.R, allowing pilot pressure at A1 and B1 to decay so the pilot-operated checks can reseat for the required low-drift hold.
Advance and return speed targets are realized by pump flow and cylinder-area sizing rather than by topology-level flow-control valves, matching the selected sizing_only motion-control decisions.
Only one carriage actuator is selected, so no synchronization topology is required.

design_decisions.decision: Use a fixed-displacement open-circuit supply with tank, pump and direct relief branch.
design_decisions.rationale: This matches the selected simple conventional topology and the deterministic open-circuit power-and-relief pattern. Tank.S feeds Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and DCV.P; ReliefValve.T and DCV.T return directly to Tank.R.
driven_by: Selected the fixed-displacement pump because no energy-efficiency or standby-unloading intent is specified and simplicity is prioritized.
Open-circuit reservoir and pump are required for the hydraulic power supply.
System overpressure protection is required at the specified 100 bar maximum.

design_decisions.decision: Use the selected spring-centred 4/3 open-centre DCV for advance, return and released neutral.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected DCV provides extend, neutral and retract states for the double-acting cylinder. Its open-centre neutral unloads the fixed-displacement pump and vents both work lines to tank, which is compatible with pilot-check load-lock reseating.
driven_by: Selected the open-centre 4/3 DCV because its neutral interconnects P, T, A and B, unloading the fixed pump and venting both pilot-check valve-side work lines.
Safe neutral with no commanded carriage motion on command release is required.

design_decisions.decision: Install the selected dual pilot-operated check valve between the DCV work ports and the cylinder ports.
design_decisions.rationale: The load lock provides free flow from valve-side ports to actuator-side ports during commanded motion and blocks reverse flow from the actuator chambers when not piloted open. Pairing it with the open-centre DCV neutral provides the required pilot pressure decay path to tank for low-leakage holding.
driven_by: Selected a dual pilot-operated check valve rather than relying on DCV spool leakage for the explicit 10 minute negligible-drift hold requirement.
Timed negligible-drift hold at any stopped position requires positive load holding.
Neutral/power-off must leave the load-supporting reverse path blocked while pilot pressure decays.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add a flow-control valve for the advance or return speeds.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected motion-control decisions classify both motion speeds as sizing_only. Therefore the topology uses direct work paths through the DCV and load lock; final pump displacement and cylinder geometry must meet the speed and force requirements.
driven_by: No flow-control valve is included; advance and return speeds are sizing-only targets per the typed motion decisions.
Numeric speed and force targets are deferred to pump/cylinder sizing and do not justify a flow-control valve.

design_decisions.decision: Do not include a counterbalance valve.
design_decisions.rationale: The typed load for advance, return and hold is resistive for a horizontal carriage. Static holding is handled by the pilot-check load lock; dynamic overrunning-load control is not specified.
driven_by: No counterbalance valve is included because the carriage load is horizontal/resistive and dynamic overrunning-load control is not specified.
Motion-control decisions specify load_type resistive and load_control none during powered advance and return.

design_decisions.decision: Represent load-lock cross-pilot release as internal conditional behavior of the selected component rather than as separate pilot-line components.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected dual pilot-operated check catalog metadata provides only ports A1, A2, B1 and B2 and declares internal conditional release paths requiring pressure at the opposite valve-side port. No separate external pilot ports are listed, so no extra pilot connections or components are added.
driven_by: Use only ports listed for each selected key.
Do not insert line, manifold, tee or other unselected components.
Selected load-lock metadata defines conditional internal cross-pilot release from pressure at A1 or B1.

assumptions: The selected dual pilot-operated check valve has internal cross-pilot passages as declared in its catalog metadata; it exposes no separate pilot or drain ports that need topology connections.
ReliefValve remains normally closed in ordinary advance, return and hold phases and opens only under overpressure; no phase command state is required by the selected catalog metadata.
Cylinder stroke, bore, rod diameter, pump displacement and relief setting are finalized during sizing and commissioning.
open_issues: Final sizing must select pump displacement and cylinder geometry to achieve the specified advance/return speeds, forces and 300 mm travel within the 100 bar system limit.
Detailed implementation must ensure the load lock is mounted close enough to the actuator work ports to meet the project interpretation of negligible drift; no numeric drift tolerance was supplied.
Final relief-valve setting and commissioning method are outside topology selection.

research_coverage.summary: The basic open-circuit power/return/relief topology is well supported. The double-acting cylinder plus spring-centered 4/3 directional valve pattern is mostly supported, and the use of pilot-operated check/load-lock valves for low-leakage static holding is supported. However, the accumulated evidence is not yet sufficient to design the complete carriage topology safely and unambiguously because two critical details remain weak: the exact neutral-center connection that both vents the pilot/check valve work lines and remains compatible with the pump/unloading strategy, and the controlled-motion/load-control choice for any overrunning or inertia-driven carriage load. Current findings support static holding with pilot-operated checks, but do not adequately establish when that is sufficient versus when counterbalance/over-center load-control valves or metering are required.

items.rationale: Findings include cited engineering guidance for reservoir-to-pump suction, pump/control/actuator/return flow path, return to reservoir, and a relief valve connected to the pressure line with outlet to reservoir/return to limit maximum system pressure. The specific 100 bar setting is a design requirement rather than an external research fact, and the evidence supports the preset-pressure principle.

The actuator and basic directional-control pattern is supported: double-acting cylinder, 3-position 4-way spring-centered DCV, P/T/A/B port assignments, and shifted advance/retract behavior. But the safe neutral is not yet fully unambiguous when combined with the load-lock valves: the holding evidence recommends cylinder/work ports connected to tank with pilot-operated checks, while the directional-control evidence separately discusses open/tandem/closed centers for pump compatibility. The missing supported claim is the exact 4/3 center configuration and pump/unloading arrangement that simultaneously vents A/B pilot lines, avoids unintended pilot pressure, and avoids unsafe/overheating blocked-pump neutral behavior.

Static load holding is supported by cited evidence for double pilot-operated check/load-lock valves in both cylinder work lines, cross-pilot release, and the inadequacy of relying on closed-center spool valves due to leakage/drift. However, the need also asks for a controlled-motion pattern. The current evidence does not establish whether pilot-operated checks alone are appropriate for the carriage’s load dynamics or whether counterbalance/over-center load-control valves, meter-out control, or other motion-control elements are required to prevent uncontrolled motion under overrunning/inertial loads.

The leak-resistant static holding topology is substantially supported: poppet/check-type load-locking is preferred over spool-only holding, double pilot-operated checks can block reverse flow on both cylinder ports, and neutral should vent work/pilot lines so the checks reseat. Still missing is a sufficiently supported neutral-center implementation with pump compatibility, and evidence tying the chosen load-holding element to controlled release/motion under the actual carriage load condition. Exact part selection and leakage-rate verification can be handled later by catalog/design calculations, but the topology-level choice between pilot-operated checks and counterbalance/load-control valves remains unresolved.

missing_or_weak_information: Exact supported neutral-center connection for the 4/3 DCV when used with double pilot-operated checks: A and B/work lines must be vented to tank in neutral so pilot pressure decays, while the pump port must be handled safely for the chosen pump type.

Whether the carriage load can become overrunning or inertia-driven, and if so whether pilot-operated checks alone are unsafe/inadequate and counterbalance or other load-control valves are required for controlled motion.

Placement guidance for load-holding/load-control valves close to or directly on the actuator is not strongly evidenced in the accumulated findings; this may be important if hose/line failure protection is part of the safety intent.

design_review.summary: The topology functionally satisfies the brief: open-circuit tank/pump/relief supply is correctly arranged with direct relief protection and returns to tank; the 4/3 open-centre DCV provides extend, retract, and released neutral paths; the dual pilot-operated check/load-lock is correctly placed between the DCV work ports and cylinder ports with opposite-line pilot release; neutral vents both valve-side work/pilot lines to tank so the checks can reseat and hold the carriage without relying on DCV spool leakage. No unjustified flow-control, counterbalance, synchronization, or sequence components are added.

No unjustified flow-control, counterbalance, synchronization, or sequence components are added.
